title: 2023年12月 第1套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hello, doctor.
lines.translation: M：你好，医生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hello, please take a seat.
lines.translation: 你好,请坐

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I have your test results here, and it's good news.
lines.translation: 我有你的测试结果,这是好消息

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The blood test came back clear.
lines.translation: 验血结果清晰

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There is no indication of any digestive issues.
lines.translation: 没有迹象表明有任何消化问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So then why do I feel so poorly all the time?
lines.translation: M：那我为什么总是感觉这么不舒服？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
lines.translation: W：这可能是过度劳累和压力造成的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No, it can't be.
lines.translation: M：不，不可能。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress.
lines.translation: 我一直都很努力地工作，但从来没有感到过压力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Other people suffering complain about that, but I don't.
lines.translation: 其他饱受压力折磨的人会抱怨这个问题，但我不会。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It must be something else.
lines.translation: 一定是别的原因。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What you have just described is a common sentiment.
lines.translation: W：你刚才描述的情况很常见。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it.
lines.translation: 许多承受压力的人都没有意识到自己正处于压力之中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You told me you often work long into the night, right?
lines.translation: 你告诉过我，你经常工作到深夜，对吧？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes, most days in fact.
lines.translation: M：对，实际上大多数日子都是这样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
lines.translation: 但我这样已经有大约20年了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That doesn't matter.
lines.translation: W：那并不代表什么。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it, and now it's catching up to you.
lines.translation: 你可能在不知情的情况下承受了20年的压力，现在它开始影响你了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
lines.translation: M：可是我总是感到疲惫，晚上也睡不好，这又是怎么回事？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Those are common consequences of stress.
lines.translation: W：这些都是压力带来的常见后果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued.
lines.translation: 如果你睡不好，当然就会感到疲劳。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you.
lines.translation: 我会给你开一些特殊的安眠药。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients, so your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects.
lines.translation: 它们药效温和，是用天然成分制成的，所以你的胃应该能够很好地耐受，也不应产生任何负面副作用。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month.
lines.translation: 晚餐时服用一片，一个月后再来见我。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
lines.translation: 如果没有改善，我会给你开药效更强的药。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thank you, doctor.
lines.translation: M：谢谢你，医生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's not all.
lines.translation: W：还不止这些。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You should try and work less.
lines.translation: 你应该试着少工作一些。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
lines.translation: 你有没有办法减轻自己的工作量？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Um, I'd have to think about it.
lines.translation: M：嗯，我得考虑一下。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive.
lines.translation: 我是一名餐厅经理，而这个行业竞争非常激烈。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
lines.translation: 有很多事情需要跟进并确保掌控。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else.
lines.translation: W：我建议你考虑把一部分职责委派给其他人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm not asking you to retire just to slow down a bit.
lines.translation: 我不是让你退休，只是让你稍微放慢节奏。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's for your own health.
lines.translation: 这是为了你自己的健康。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 1-4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题1 -4是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. What do we learn about the man from his test results?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：从男士的检查结果中我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：女士认为许多人当中有什么普遍现象?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What does the woman say she will do for the man?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：女士说她将为男士做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：男士对他所从事的行业说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Today, on People in the News, our guest is John Williams.
lines.translation: 欢迎收看今天的《新闻人物》，我们的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player.
lines.translation: 这个名字大家可能不太熟悉，但约翰曾经是一位备受赞誉的篮球运动员。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25.
lines.translation: 约翰，你在年仅25岁时退役让球迷们大吃一惊。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why did you retire so early?
lines.translation: 你当时为什么这么早就选择退役呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity.
lines.translation: 梅格，我热爱成为一名运动员，但我不喜欢成为名人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake.
lines.translation: 我还在上高中时就处于聚光灯下，高中一毕业就转为了职业球员，这其实是个错误。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
lines.translation: 我当时是个害羞的孩子，还没做好应对所有媒体关注的准备。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary.
lines.translation: 但在职业生涯鼎盛时期放弃数百万美元，大多数人都无法抵挡如此高薪的诱惑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
lines.translation: 当你离开赛场时，外界曾推测你是和队友产生了矛盾，甚至是有伤在身。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Not at all.
lines.translation: 完全不是这样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was hard to quit.
lines.translation: 选择放弃确实很难。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I was tempted to stay in the game, because I love basketball and I loved my team.
lines.translation: 我当时也纠结过要不要留下来继续打球，因为我热爱篮球，也热爱我的球队。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As for money, I turned professional at 18.
lines.translation: 至于钱的问题，我18岁就转为了职业球员。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisers.
lines.translation: 因为我有优秀的理财顾问，所以我实际上已经赚了不少钱，并且存下了大部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
lines.translation: 我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球并不是一项能打很久的职业，所以我希望趁自己还年轻转换职业。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news.
lines.translation: 好的，那是20年前的事了，现在你又重回大众视野。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports.
lines.translation: 你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why?
lines.translation: 这是为什么呢？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities.
lines.translation: 我读了大学，学习了公共卫生学，了解到肥胖流行问题的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年群体中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem.
lines.translation: 在过去二十年里，我一直在努力缓解这个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The foundation is just the latest attempt.
lines.translation: 这个基金会只是我最新的尝试。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
lines.translation: 这个基金会利用私人捐款来资助小学的男女生篮球队，对吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too, and also have some public funding.
lines.translation: 实际上，我们也资助中学生的球队，而且我们也有一些公共资金。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 5-8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题5 -8是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：John Williams 为什么在年仅 25 岁时就离开了篮球运动?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：关于篮球作为大多数球员的职业,这位男士说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：关于 20 年后的 John Williams,我们从这位女士那里了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. What has the man spent the last two decades trying to do?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：这位男士在过去二十年里一直试图做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B,
lines.translation: B节,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: directions.
lines.translation: 方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you will hear two passages.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到两段。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在每一段的结尾 你会听到三个或四个问题

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 发言的通过和提问将只讲一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices mark A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 在听到一个问题后,你必须从四个选项A、B、C和D中选择最佳答案。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one
lines.translation: 答题表一中对应的字母

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: with a the sensor.
lines.translation: 与感应器。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951.
lines.translation: 凯特·阿特金森于1951年出生于英国约克。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author.
lines.translation: 她努力获得了作为作家的资历。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She studied English Literature at University in Scotland.
lines.translation: 她在苏格兰的一所大学学习英国文学。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature.
lines.translation: 1974年毕业后，她攻读美国文学博士学位。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981.
lines.translation: 后来，她在自己毕业的那所大学任教，并于1981年开始创作短篇小说。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.
lines.translation: 她赢得1986年《Woman's Own》短篇小说比赛后，开始为女性杂志撰稿。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award.
lines.translation: 她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》获得了1995年英国年度图书奖。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV.
lines.translation: 小说以约克郡为背景，后来被改编成广播剧、舞台剧和电视剧。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh—the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
lines.translation: 她为爱丁堡的一家剧院创作了两部戏剧，第一部名为《Nice》，第二部名为《Abandonment》，于2000年8月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分演出。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.
lines.translation: 无论阿特金森创作哪一种类型的作品，她的书都触及爱与失去以及如何继续生活下去等主题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor.
lines.translation: 她总是以独具匠心的方式呈现这些主题，并带有一种辛辣的幽默感。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized.
lines.translation: 她的书中往往充满古怪、有时甚至有罪过、总体上存在缺陷的特立独行者；正因为这些人物被刻画得如此完整，他们才显得可信。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners.
lines.translation: 她的书经常被称为风俗喜剧。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character.
lines.translation: 也就是说，这类喜剧描绘的是社会时尚圈中复杂而精致的行为规范，在那里，外表比真正的道德品质更重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds.
lines.translation: 风俗喜剧往往奖赏那些聪明而诡诈的人物，而不是惩罚他们的恶行。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
lines.translation: 风俗喜剧的幽默依靠语言机智和顽皮的调侃。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：Kate Atkinson 是什么时候开始为女性杂志撰稿的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：Kate Atkinson 的书涉及了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：关于风尚喜剧中聪明而狡诈的角色,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
lines.translation: 为什么说适应能力是在职场中需要培养的一项重要技能？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.
lines.translation: 简单来说，适应能力是雇主日益重视的一项技能。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.
lines.translation: 当你花时间学习一项新任务，而不是抗拒它时，你的工作效率就会提高。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward.
lines.translation: 你还可以为那些在适应方面可能遇到困难的同事树立榜样，并帮助带领团队向前发展。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark, explains it to us this way.
lines.translation: 战略顾问多莉·克拉克这样向我们解释：“我认为，适应能力之所以是职场中的一项重要技能，是因为坦率地说，环境会发生变化。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because frankly, circumstances change.
lines.translation: 竞争对手会推出新产品，经济可能会陷入衰退，客户偏好会随着时间而改变，等等。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Competitors introduce new products, economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more.
lines.translation: 如果你对着天空挥拳，问为什么不能一成不变，那不会带来什么实际帮助。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you shake your fist at the sky and say why can't it stay the same, that's not going to do very much good.
lines.translation: 相反，你需要认识到环境已经发生变化，从而根据现实情况，而不是根据你希望世界呈现的样子，采取适当行动。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed, so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be.
lines.translation: 这样一来，你就能作出更准确、更有依据且更有效的选择。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices."

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Also, the workplace itself has been evolving.
lines.translation: 此外，职场本身也一直在不断发展变化。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.
lines.translation: 如今的职场文化和管理方式通常以团队合作为基础，而不是建立在僵化的等级制度之上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique.
lines.translation: 头脑风暴要求具备创造力、灵活性和情商，是一种典型的问题解决方法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company.
lines.translation: 无法或不愿参与的员工，很难在公司中顺利发展。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.
lines.translation: 灵活变通的员工还展现出其他技能。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working.
lines.translation: 他们能够在发生变化时迅速调整优先事项，并在某件事不起作用时提出进一步的修改建议。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
lines.translation: 当遭遇挫折时，他们也能迅速重新组织起来，自信地适应新情况，而不会反应过度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：为什么说话者认为适应能力是在职场中需要锻炼的一项重要技能?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：根据战略顾问Dorie Clark的说法,适应能力使我们能够做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：从文中我们对当今的工作文化了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：当变化发生时,具有适应能力的员工能够做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在本节中,各位将听取三场讲座或会谈录音,然后是三四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The recordings will be played only once.
lines.translation: 录音只播放一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices, Mark A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 你听到一个问题, 你必须从四个选择中选择最好的答案, 马克A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 1 What makes humans different from other species?
lines.translation: 记录1 是什么使人类有别于其他物种?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What makes humans different from other species?
lines.translation: 是什么使人类区别于其他物种？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development.
lines.translation: 一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家断言是我们更高的认知发展水平。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.
lines.translation: 但我认为，主要区别在于我们渴望对抗惯常模式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
lines.translation: 这使创造具有生物学意义上的必然性，因为我们在艺术和技术中寻求的是惊喜，而不只是满足预期。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species.
lines.translation: 因此，狂野的想象力贯穿了我们这个物种的历史。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols, and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design.
lines.translation: 我们建造精巧复杂的栖息地，为食物设计复杂的食谱，穿着体现时尚不断变化的服装，用繁复的标志、符号和声音进行交流，还乘坐由我们自己设计的翅膀和轮子，在不同栖息地之间往来。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key.
lines.translation: 为了满足我们对新奇事物的渴望，创新至关重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But who innovates?
lines.translation: 但谁在创新？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate.
lines.translation: 如今，许多人，包括普通人和专家，都认为只有天才才能创新。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do.
lines.translation: 但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才会做的事情。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next.
lines.translation: 创新的驱动力存在于每个人的大脑中，而由此产生的反重复之战，正是推动巨大变革的力量，使一代人与下一代人彼此不同。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The drive to create the new is a trait of being human.
lines.translation: 创造新事物的动力是人类特有的特征。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions.
lines.translation: 我们成百上千地建立文化，以数百万计讲述新的故事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not.
lines.translation: 我们创造并置身于此前从未存在过的事物之中，而动物不会这样做。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But where do our new ideas come from?
lines.translation: 但我们的新思想究竟从何而来？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds.
lines.translation: 许多人认为，新思想会凭空出现在伟大思想家的脑海中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic.
lines.translation: 从这个角度看，新思想几乎像是魔法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few.
lines.translation: 它们以灵感闪现的方式降临到少数人身上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process.
lines.translation: 然而，现实是，在人类活动的各个领域，先前的工作推动着创造过程。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further.
lines.translation: 我们可能认为创新源于灵感或天才，但实际上，它是进一步发展他人思想的结果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions.
lines.translation: 这种情况发生在技术领域：一项发明会促成或启发更多发明。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work.
lines.translation: 在艺术领域也是如此，作家、作曲家和画家会将前辈艺术家的作品运用到自己的创作中。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The human brain works from precedent.
lines.translation: 人类大脑以先例为基础运作。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
lines.translation: 我们吸收继承而来的思想，并将它们重新组合成某种新的形式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What is a true creator?
lines.translation: 什么是真正的创造者？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing?
lines.translation: 创造者是那个能从无到有创造出某种事物的天才吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No.
lines.translation: 不是。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures.
lines.translation: 创造者只不过是运用继承之物、吸收过去并加以改造，从而创造出未来可能性的人类。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.
lines.translation: 因此，人类通常都是创造者，而不是只有少数例外者。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. What question does the speaker address in this talk?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：演讲者在本次讲话中探讨了什么问题?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. What does the speaker believe about innovation?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：演讲者对创新有何看法?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. How does the human brain work according to the speaker?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：根据演讲者的说法,人类大脑是如何运作的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Many dog owners will tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition,
lines.translation: 许多狗主人会告诉你,他们的狗不知何故知道 他们什么时候生病或心烦意乱, 根据研究狗认知的研究人员,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time.
lines.translation: 狗确实知道它们的人类伴侣正经历艰难时期。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions.
lines.translation: 你的狗不仅能察觉你感冒了，家犬还表现出了发现细微情绪波动以及更严重身体状况的能力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change.
lines.translation: 这是因为狗对熟悉之人的变化极其敏感，而疾病会引起变化。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
lines.translation: 例如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，他的气味就会异常；即使人类自己察觉不到这种变化，狗也能闻出来，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell.
lines.translation: 研究人员还发现，一个人的情绪可能是更严重疾病的迹象，并会触发狗的嗅觉。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well.
lines.translation: 人类的情绪会以身体释放出的化学信号在生理上表现出来，而狗同样能够闻到这些信号。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.
lines.translation: 除了嗅觉之外，狗还会从人的声音中获取信息，以察觉变化。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone.
lines.translation: 2014年，研究人员发现，狗的大脑中有一个区域与人类大脑中的某个区域相似，使它们能够理解说话者声音语调中的情绪线索，而不仅仅是从熟悉的词语中获取信息。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness.
lines.translation: 一个人的声音也可能携带疾病的迹象。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes.
lines.translation: 人们目前还不太清楚狗究竟理解这些变化到了什么程度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear.
lines.translation: 人类会发出许多线索，但狗是否知道其中一些线索意味着疾病，还不明确。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
lines.translation: 我们认为狗表现出的关切，可能更像是它们对我们出了问题这一情况产生了更强的好奇或怀疑，而待在我们身边则是获取更多相关信息的好方法。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer.
lines.translation: 一些研究人员断言，狗有朝一日将帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经展现出检测多种疾病的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future.
lines.translation: 但这些研究人员也承认，那可能是遥远未来的事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself.
lines.translation: 目前的研究表明，养狗本身就能带来一系列益处。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood.
lines.translation: 事实证明，饲养宠物狗有助于增进健康、改善情绪。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
lines.translation: 狗还能帮助人放松，对于患有慢性疾病的人来说，它们尤其能带来安慰。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. What view of many dog owners win support from researchers studying dog cognition?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：研究犬类认知的研究人员支持许多养狗者的哪种观点?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. Why can dogs detect their owner's abnormal odor according to the speaker?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：根据说话者所述,狗为什么能察觉主人的异常气味?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What does research suggest for now about dog ownership?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：目前研究对养狗有何提示?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 3.
lines.translation: 记录3。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Earlier this month, the think tank called onward published a report, a question of degree.
lines.translation: 本月早些时候,智囊团呼吁继续发表一份报告,一个学位问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.
lines.translation: Onward 认为，部长们应当“严厉整治那些在学生毕业十年后仍只能为其提供极低性价比的课程”；如果此类课程的毕业生平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛，就应限制这些课程招收新生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored.
lines.translation: 对于科学、技术、工程、数学以及经济学等专业，由于其毕业生平均收入较高，则应予以优先考虑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money.
lines.translation: 这份报告为政府正在进行的一项审查提供了参考，该审查旨在研究如何改革技术教育，以及如何确保学生获得良好的性价比。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.
lines.translation: 乍看之下，Onward 似乎确实有道理。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, ten years after graduation.
lines.translation: 根据其数据，大多数创意艺术类学生在毕业十年后年收入低于25,000英镑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university.
lines.translation: 事实上，据称创意艺术类专业的男性学生平均收入远低于他们如果当初根本没有上大学所能获得的收入。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This isn't really good for anyone, and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
lines.translation: 这对任何人来说都不利，对毕业生而言尤其如此，因为他们被迫忍受一种永远无法攒下钱、永远买不起房、永远不敢指望退休的生活方式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Onward has identified a real problem.
lines.translation: Onward 确实发现了一个真实存在的问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students—have fairly good work prospects.
lines.translation: 顶尖大学的创意艺术类毕业生，例如牛津大学的毕业生，由于其中有很大一部分学生来自私立学校，因此往往拥有相当不错的就业前景。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation.
lines.translation: 可是，所有毕业生中有40%——无论他们所学的是什么学位——在毕业五年后年收入低于25,000英镑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
lines.translation: 这表明，问题其实并不在于某些特定学生攻读某些特定学位，而在于整个经济状况。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
lines.translation: 无论年轻人学了什么，除非他们足够幸运，出生在拥有成功事业的家庭，否则都很难取得进展。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world.
lines.translation: 如果部长们希望让教育为年轻人带来回报，就需要把视野放在高等教育领域之外，转向更广阔的社会。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The rewards that education gives us are not measurable.
lines.translation: 教育带给我们的回报是无法衡量的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct.
lines.translation: 它们并不总是立刻显现出来，当然也并不总是直接的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it.
lines.translation: 接受教育会让你成为一个不同于未接受教育时的自己的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life.
lines.translation: 我们需要从人生的角度，而不是从银行账户余额的角度，来审视教育的价值。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.
lines.translation: 如果我们继续让自己被“性价比”之类的说法分散注意力，最终我们所有人的生活都会因此变得更加贫乏。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What does Onward's report propose ministers should do?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：Onward的报告建议部长们应该做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What does the speaker think of Onward's arguments?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：说话者如何看待Onward的论点?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：关于英国大学毕业生毕业五年后的情况,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：说话者认为什么实际上是Onward所指出问题的原因?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
